incidents.vector: Attackers chained two zero-days (CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410) in SonicWall SMA1000 remote-access appliances, going from no access to full appliance compromise; exploitation began June 22, roughly three weeks before patches shipped.
incidents.impact: SonicWall confirmed multiple cases of active exploitation across a fleet of under 5,000 SMA1000 units; Rapid7 assessed the goal was ransomware and blocked encryption and data theft in the cases it observed. CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

incidents.victim: On-premises Microsoft SharePoint and Active Directory Federation Services users
incidents.vector: Two privilege-escalation zero-days disclosed in July Patch Tuesday are being exploited in the wild: CVE-2026-56164 in on-prem SharePoint Server and CVE-2026-56155 in AD FS; post-exploitation includes stealing IIS machine keys and deploying webshells for persistence.
incidents.impact: CISA issued SharePoint hardening guidance and added the flaws to its KEV catalog, giving federal agencies until July 17-28 to remediate. Both were found by Microsoft's incident-response unit amid a record 622-CVE Patch Tuesday.

incidents.victim: Poland energy grid and European critical infrastructure
incidents.vector: A December 2025 cyberattack that nearly caused a blackout affecting heating for half a million Poles was formally attributed to the FSB's signals-intelligence arm (Center 16), part of a broader sabotage and espionage campaign against critical infrastructure in at least ten European countries; a 13-nation advisory warned the same actor is scanning the internet for network devices with default or weak credentials.
incidents.impact: The UK and EU imposed their first coordinated cyber sanctions on Russia, targeting 30+ individuals and entities including intelligence officers and the operators of Lumma Stealer. France summoned the Russian ambassador. Water-treatment facilities in Poland were also targeted, posing a direct risk to water supply.

incidents.vector: Actors using tradecraft associated with ShinyHunters abused trusted OAuth relationships to reach customer Salesforce instances via three paths: vishing employees into authorizing a malicious 'Data Loader' app, compromising third-party integrations (Salesloft Drift, Gainsight, and market-intelligence firm Klue), and exploiting misconfigured guest access to Aura/GraphQL endpoints.
incidents.impact: Attackers enumerated and mass-exfiltrated CRM records (accounts, contacts, case data) across many tenants while evading traditional sign-in detections. Microsoft worked with Salesforce to add near-real-time OAuth telemetry to Defender for Cloud Apps.

incidents.vector: Attackers stole Lidl customer data from an external service provider, a third-party supply-chain compromise rather than a breach of Lidl's own systems.
incidents.impact: Customer data belonging to the discount retailer was taken; scope and downstream use were not yet detailed at disclosure.

incidents.victim: NATO military-logistics routes and Ukrainian military personnel
incidents.vector: Russian intelligence systematically compromised internet-connected security cameras across the Netherlands, other NATO/EU states, and Ukraine by exploiting default passwords, outdated firmware, and default configurations, then used image-recognition software to analyze feeds for military vehicles and cargo.
incidents.impact: Dutch intelligence agencies (AIVD/MIVD) warned that hacked cameras tracked weapons shipments to Ukraine and, in some cases, helped locate Ukrainian soldiers for lethal strikes; a small number of compromised cameras were also found along Dutch military transport routes.

incidents.vector: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service program (active since mid-2025, offering affiliates an unusual 90% payout) gains initial access via edge-device exploits, brute force, stolen credentials, and initial-access brokers, then uses custom Go/C encryptors, an EDR-killer framework, and a suspected zero-day.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 tracked 580 claimed victims across 77 countries since inception, 103 of them in manufacturing, with June 2026 its highest month (117 victims) — making it the second most active RaaS operation of 2026.

incidents.victim: Website owners and small/medium businesses worldwide (many in Australia)
incidents.vector: A large-scale campaign scans for and exploits roughly 17 known vulnerabilities in content management systems and plugins (WordPress, Craft CMS, Joomla, and others) allowing unauthenticated file upload, RCE, SSRF, or deserialization, then deploys webshells for remote control.
incidents.impact: Australia's ACSC issued a critical alert warning that compromised web servers are being used for defacement, credential capture, malware distribution, and as a pathway to broader network compromise; many Australian SMBs were impacted.

incidents.vector: A modular Golang implant dubbed GigaWiper (tracked as BlueRabbit) combines a full-featured backdoor (~20 C2 commands over RabbitMQ/Redis) with three on-demand destructive modules: a raw-disk wiper, fake ransomware that discards encryption keys, and a multipass secure file wiper.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Threat Intelligence spotted the malware during destructive wiper activity in October 2025; Binary Defense attributed BlueRabbit to an Iran-based actor. The design lets attackers choose whether and how to destroy a system after establishing control, minimizing operational footprint.

incidents.victim: Consumers and small/medium businesses (US and EU)
incidents.vector: A financially motivated Vidar-stealer affiliate uses malvertising for fake cracked-software downloads, delivering Factory-v3-built Go loaders signed with a fabricated JustWatch certificate and padded with hundreds of MB of null bytes to evade sandboxes; the loader drops Vidar stealer and the XMRig cryptominer after an AMSI bypass.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 saw a spike in the campaign from mid-to-late April 2026; Vidar harvests browser credentials, cookies, and crypto wallets while XMRig mines Monero on victim machines. The same builder and certificate infrastructure underpins a concurrent Lumma stealer campaign.

incidents.victim: Consumer IoT devices worldwide (NetNut / Popa botnet)
incidents.vector: The NetNut residential-proxy network (aka Popa), estimated at 2M+ devices, enrolled home devices such as smart TVs and streaming boxes as proxy exit nodes via malicious SDKs, renting the hijacked IPs to others for scraping, ad fraud, account takeover, and to mask cybercriminal and espionage traffic.
incidents.impact: The FBI, Google, and Lumen seized hundreds of NetNut domains and disabled Google-hosted C2, degrading the network by millions of devices; in one week GTIG had observed 316 distinct threat clusters (including espionage groups) using NetNut exit nodes.

incidents.vector: The pro-Ukraine hacktivist group Cyber Anarchy Squad breached one of Russia's largest construction companies, wiping servers and workstations and deleting all backups.
incidents.impact: The group claims it wiped roughly 3,000 servers and workstations plus 700 virtual machines and stole more than 650 TB of documents. The May breach was disclosed only in late June.

incidents.vector: The Qilin ransomware group breached the Central Bank of Libya's network; officials traced the intrusion to an incident roughly three weeks before stolen files were leaked.
incidents.impact: Files allegedly taken from the central bank were published on the dark web; Libyan authorities opened an investigation.

incidents.vector: Attackers stole customer data from the Japanese branch of insurer Aflac; the specific intrusion vector was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: More than 4.38 million customers were affected — the company's second disclosed breach in about a year.

incidents.vector: A newly launched ransomware group calling itself BLackField hit Nidec, forcing the company to take its entire IT network offline.
incidents.impact: The group demanded a $2 million ransom from the motor and electronic-components maker, which had also suffered a ransomware attack in late 2024.

incidents.vector: The World Leaks data-extortion group breached Apple supplier Tata Electronics and, after the company refused to pay, leaked roughly 200,000 documents.
incidents.impact: The leak exposed images of the unreleased iPhone 18 and its components, including battery, chips, and circuit boards — a supply-chain leak of pre-release product designs.

incidents.victim: US Department of Homeland Security (Homeland Security Information Network)
incidents.vector: Intruders breached HSIN — a DHS network for sharing sensitive data with federal, state, local, and industry partners — targeting HSIN servers and a connected SharePoint system between late May and early June.
incidents.impact: The intrusion hit a sensitive government information-sharing platform; the identity of the attackers and what data was taken remain unknown.

incidents.vector: The ShinyHunters group hacked the US insurance sector's standards body at the start of June, prompting some credit-rating agencies to pause data sharing to avoid exposing sensitive data.
incidents.impact: NAIC suspended risk designations that tell insurers how much capital they need to cover policies; it says it has since evicted the intruders and is restoring operations with credit agencies.
